hero.title: Anki
hero.lead: ankika is a terminal client for Anki that syncs with AnkiWeb. It doesn't need Anki installed. It's built on Anki's own Rust core, so cards are scheduled the same way as in Anki.
hero.tryIt: Click the terminal, then press <kbd>Space</kbd> and <kbd>1</kbd> to <kbd>4</kbd>.

demo.label: ankika review screen. Press Space to show the answer, then 1 to 4 to answer.
demo.congratulations: Congratulations! You have finished this deck for now.

sync.title: Syncs with AnkiWeb
sync.lead: Log in with your AnkiWeb account to sync cards, review history and media with Anki on your other devices. A self-hosted anki-sync-server works as well.

points.when: Syncs on startup, after login and before quitting
points.keyring: The login is stored in the system keyring

features.title: What it covers
features.lead: Cards are rendered from their HTML, so formatting, clozes, images and sound are kept. Most of what you do in Anki day to day is there as well.

images.title: Images in the card
images.body: Pictures show inline in terminals that support them, and as colored blocks everywhere else.

audio.title: Audio playback
audio.body: Sounds play on their own when the deck says so. Replay them with one key, or click a sound to hear it.

typeIn.title: Type-in answers
typeIn.body: Type the answer and get the same comparison Anki shows, clozes included.

notes.title: Add and edit notes
notes.body: Pick a note type and deck, then write the fields in your $EDITOR. While reviewing, <kbd>e</kbd> opens the current note.

browser.title: Card browser
browser.body: Search with Anki's own search syntax, then flag, suspend, bury or move cards in bulk.

stats.title: Statistics
stats.body: Today, future due, reviews, a year's calendar and true retention, drawn as charts in the terminal.

palette.title: Command palette
palette.body: Find any action by fuzzy search. The footer lists the keys for the current screen.

packages.title: Import and export
packages.body: Import shared decks and export decks or the whole collection, from the TUI or the command line.

options.title: Your settings, kept
options.body: Deck options with FSRS, custom study and separate profiles work like they do in Anki.

scripting.title: Commands for scripts
scripting.lead: Besides the full-screen app, ankika has commands for status bars, timers and shell scripts. --json prints the output as JSON.

due.title: Cards due, in your status bar
due.body: For waybar, polybar, tmux or a shell prompt. --deck counts a single deck.

sync.title: Sync on a timer
sync.body: Run ankika sync from cron or a systemd timer. Completions and a man page are included.

install.title: Install
install.lead: Download a release binary or build it yourself. Run ankika and log in from the command palette to sync.

release.note: For Linux (x86_64), macOS (Apple silicon) and Windows (x86_64). Each archive has the binary, shell completions and the man page.

arch.note: Installs completions for bash, zsh and fish, and the man page.

cargo.note: Needs the latest stable Rust and protoc. On Linux, audio also needs ALSA's development files.

footer.label: Links
footer.notice: Free software under the AGPL-3.0. ankika is an independent project and isn't affiliated with Anki or AnkiWeb.
